root_idea.summary: The root is centered on بَصَل, the onion, a known bulbous plant.
root_idea.development: The onion's layered coats motivate Classical extensions involving many-fold structure, thick or multilayered coverings, and a helmet; related derived verbs also express stripping and figurative exhaustion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Standalone Quran-attested noun, presented under the normalized lexical citation form بَصَل.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic food-list expression وَبَصَلِهَا, “and its onions,” in 2:61.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of stripping or divesting; to strip someone of clothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun for the Form II usage بَصَّلَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become several-fold or many-fold, like the coats of an onion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive derived-verb usage describing increased multiplicity or layered form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be importuned until one's possessions are exhausted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative transitive usage in which repeated begging exhausts what a person has.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bulb or bulbous plant, including various wild bulbs such as squill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader botanical use than the ordinary onion designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pointed iron helmet, named by resemblance to an onion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Classical use based on the form of the onion and its projecting middle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covering consisting of many coats; thick or multilayered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective or participial description of something having numerous coverings, by comparison with onion layers.
